chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I said to Al-Reza (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you! Supplicate to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that He should grant me the halal (permissible sustenance).' He said, 'Do you know what is the halal?' I said, 'That which is with us, the goodly earnings.' He said, 'Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: The halal is the sustenance of the Chosen ones.' Then he said, 'Say, I ask You from Your extensive sustenance.'

key_terms.الْحَلَالُ: The permissible; specifically referring to lawful sustenance or provision in this context
key_terms.الْكَسْبُ الطَّيِّبُ: Goodly earnings; the common understanding of lawful income
key_terms.رِزْقِكَ الْوَاسِعِ: Your extensive sustenance; the specific phrase for supplication
key_terms.قُوتُ الْمُصْطَفَيْنَ: The sustenance of the Chosen ones; a spiritual definition of halal

ai.seo_question: What is the true definition of halal sustenance according to Imam Al-Reza?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (AS) elevates the concept of *halal* from mere legal permissibility to a spiritual state of being among the 'chosen ones' (*al-mustafayn*), linking sustenance to divine election. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the qualitative, spiritual dimension of provision (*rizq*) rather than just its quantitative or juridical aspects. The Imam’s instruction to ask for 'broad sustenance' underscores the belief that true *halal* is a comprehensive blessing encompassing both material and spiritual well-being.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr who said,

‘I said to Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Supplicate to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic that He<sup>azwj</sup> should Grace me the Permissibles sustenance’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do you know what is the Permissible?’ I said, ‘That which is with us, the goodly earnings’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Ali Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘The Permissible, it is the subsistenance of the Chosen ones’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Say, ‘I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> from Your<sup>azwj</sup> Extensive sustenance’’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr who has said the following: “

Once I said to al-Rida (a.s.) ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause. Pray to Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, to grant me lawful sustenance.’ The Imam said, ‘Do you know what lawful sustenance is?’ I said, ‘That which we earn and is pure.’ The Imam said that Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) would say, ‘Lawful sustenance is the sustenance of the chosen ones.’ The Imam then instructed me to say, ‘I plead before You for Your vast sustenance.’”
